\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{दाख़िल} (dākhil)}{दाख़िल (dākhil)}]{\hi{दाख़िल} (dākhil) — admitted; entered}

\label{lesson:HI-C491-dakhil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to pick at, then the Hindi for a scar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{दाख़िल}}
\textbf{\hi{दाख़िल}} — \emph{dākhil} — \textquotedblleft{}admitted; entered\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{तेज़} \hi{बुख़ार} \hi{की} \hi{वजह} \hi{से} \hi{दादा} \hi{अस्पताल} \hi{में} \hi{दाख़िल} \hi{हैं।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tez bukhār kī vajah se dādā aspatāl meṁ dākhil haiṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather is in hospital with a high fever.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{दाख़िल}} (\emph{dākhil}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{dākhil}, \textquotedblleft{}entering, inside\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian. \emph{aspatāl meṁ dākhil honā} is to be admitted to hospital.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dākhil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dākhil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tez bukhār kī vajah se dādā aspatāl meṁ dākhil haiṁ.} — Grandfather is in hospital with a high fever.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to pick at, then the Hindi for a scar, then say \emph{dākhil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{दाख़िल} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Admitted; entered\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{वार्ड} (vārḍ)}{वार्ड (vārḍ)}]{\hi{वार्ड} (vārḍ) — a hospital ward}

\label{lesson:HI-C491-vard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a scar, then the Hindi for admitted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{वार्ड}}
\textbf{\hi{वार्ड}} — \emph{vārḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}a hospital ward\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{दादा} \hi{का} \hi{बिस्तर} \hi{वार्ड} \hi{के} \hi{कोने} \hi{में} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā kā bistar vārḍ ke kone meṁ hai.}

Masculine.

\textbf{\hi{वार्ड}} (\emph{vārḍ}) is borrowed from English \emph{ward}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{स्ट्रेचर} (sṭrecar)}{स्ट्रेचर (sṭrecar)}]{\hi{स्ट्रेचर} (sṭrecar) — a stretcher}

Before the new one: say the Hindi for admitted, then the Hindi for a hospital ward.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{स्ट्रेचर}}
\textbf{\hi{स्ट्रेचर}} — \emph{sṭrecar} — \textquotedblleft{}a stretcher\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{बुलवाना} (bulvānā)}{बुलवाना (bulvānā)}]{\hi{बुलवाना} (bulvānā) — to have someone sent for}

\label{lesson:HI-C491-bulvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a hospital ward, then the Hindi for a stretcher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बुलवाना}}
\textbf{\hi{बुलवाना}} — \emph{bulvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to have someone sent for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{दादा} \hi{की} \hi{तबीयत} \hi{बिगड़ी}, \hi{तो} \hi{मीरा} \hi{ने} \hi{डाक्टर} \hi{को} \hi{बुलवाया।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā kī tabīyat bigṛī, to Mīrā ne ḍākṭar ko bulvāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When my grandfather took a turn for the worse, Mira sent for the doctor.
\end{quote}

Past, with \hi{ने} (he or she …): \hi{उसने} \hi{डाक्टर} \hi{को} \hi{बुलवाया}, \emph{usne ḍākṭar ko bulvāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{बुलवाना}} (\emph{bulvānā}) is the second causative of \emph{bolnā}: \emph{bulānā} is \textquotedblleft{}to call\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{bulvānā} is \textquotedblleft{}to get someone else to call\textquotedblright{} a person. CDIAL lists \emph{bulānā} under \emph{*bōll}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 9321).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bulvānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bulvānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā kī tabīyat bigṛī, to Mīrā ne ḍākṭar ko bulvāyā.} — When my grandfather took a turn for the worse, Mira sent for the doctor.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a hospital ward, then the Hindi for a stretcher, then say \emph{bulvānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बुलवाना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To have someone sent for\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{जान} (jān)}{जान (jān)}]{\hi{जान} (jān) — a life; the life in a body}

\label{lesson:HI-C491-jan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a stretcher, then the Hindi for to have someone sent for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{जान}}
\textbf{\hi{जान}} — \emph{jān} — \textquotedblleft{}a life; the life in a body\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{डाक्टरों} \hi{ने} \hi{बच्चे} \hi{की} \hi{जान} \hi{बचाई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍākṭaroṁ ne bacce kī jān bacāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctors saved the child's life.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{जान}} (\emph{jān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{jān}, \textquotedblleft{}life, soul\textquotedblright{}. \emph{jān bacānā} is to save a life; \emph{jīvan} is life as a span of years, \emph{jān} the life in a body.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭaroṁ ne bacce kī jān bacāī.} — The doctors saved the child's life.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a stretcher, then the Hindi for to have someone sent for, then say \emph{jān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{जान} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A life; the life in a body\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Getting Ready to In Hospital}

\label{lesson:HI-R491-review-484-491}



\begin{quote}
Say the Hindi for a twig toothbrush and to have (something) cut.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a twig toothbrush, to have (something) cut, to bathe someone, to rub in, a razor
  \item indigestion, a faint, dysentery, to retch, a burp
  \item to ache, the calf of the leg, to throb with pain, the spine, to swell (of the body)
  \item contagion, an infection, measles, smallpox, to fester
  \item a check-up, a prescription, a nurse, to have (something) looked at, to have something done
  \item to dissolve, to give (a baby) something to lick, a dose, an ointment, a herbal brew
  \item a blister from rubbing, a stitch, a scab, to pick at, a scar
  \item admitted, a hospital ward, a stretcher, to have someone sent for, a life
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A twig toothbrush? (\textbf{\hi{दातुन}}, \emph{dātun}.) To have (something) cut? (\textbf{\hi{कटवाना}}, \emph{kaṭvānā}.) To bathe someone? (\textbf{\hi{नहलाना}}, \emph{nahlānā}.) To rub in? (\textbf{\hi{मलना}}, \emph{malnā}.) A razor? (\textbf{\hi{उस्तरा}}, \emph{ustarā}.) Indigestion? (\textbf{\hi{बदहज़मी}}, \emph{badhazmī}.) A faint? (\textbf{\hi{मूर्छा}}, \emph{mūrchā}.) Dysentery? (\textbf{\hi{पेचिश}}, \emph{peciś}.) To retch? (\textbf{\hi{उबकना}}, \emph{ubaknā}.) A burp? (\textbf{\hi{डकार}}, \emph{ḍakār}.) To ache? (\textbf{\hi{दुखना}}, \emph{dukhnā}.) The calf of the leg? (\textbf{\hi{पिंडली}}, \emph{piṇḍlī}.) To throb with pain? (\textbf{\hi{कसकना}}, \emph{kasaknā}.) The spine? (\textbf{\hi{रीढ़}}, \emph{rīṛh}.) To swell (of the body)? (\textbf{\hi{सूजना}}, \emph{sūjnā}.) Contagion? (\textbf{\hi{छूत}}, \emph{chūt}.) An infection? (\textbf{\hi{संक्रमण}}, \emph{saṅkramaṇ}.) Measles? (\textbf{\hi{खसरा}}, \emph{khasrā}.) Smallpox? (\textbf{\hi{चेचक}}, \emph{cecak}.) To fester? (\textbf{\hi{पकना}}, \emph{paknā}.) A check-up? (\textbf{\hi{जाँच}}, \emph{jā̃c}.) A prescription? (\textbf{\hi{नुस्ख़ा}}, \emph{nuskhā}.) A nurse? (\textbf{\hi{नर्स}}, \emph{nars}.) To have (something) looked at? (\textbf{\hi{दिखवाना}}, \emph{dikhvānā}.) To have something done? (\textbf{\hi{कराना}}, \emph{karānā}.) To dissolve? (\textbf{\hi{घोलना}}, \emph{gholnā}.) To give (a baby) something to lick? (\textbf{\hi{चटाना}}, \emph{caṭānā}.) A dose? (\textbf{\hi{ख़ुराक}}, \emph{khurāk}.) An ointment? (\textbf{\hi{मरहम}}, \emph{marham}.) A herbal brew? (\textbf{\hi{काढ़ा}}, \emph{kāṛhā}.) A blister from rubbing? (\textbf{\hi{छाला}}, \emph{chālā}.) A stitch? (\textbf{\hi{टाँका}}, \emph{ṭā̃kā}.) A scab? (\textbf{\hi{पपड़ी}}, \emph{papṛī}.) To pick at? (\textbf{\hi{कुरेदना}}, \emph{kurednā}.) A scar? (\textbf{\hi{दाग़}}, \emph{dāġ}.) Admitted? (\textbf{\hi{दाख़िल}}, \emph{dākhil}.) A hospital ward? (\textbf{\hi{वार्ड}}, \emph{vārḍ}.) A stretcher? (\textbf{\hi{स्ट्रेचर}}, \emph{sṭrecar}.) To have someone sent for? (\textbf{\hi{बुलवाना}}, \emph{bulvānā}.) A life? (\textbf{\hi{जान}}, \emph{jān}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
